recap.title: index.js is the entry point
recap.body: Its top-level code runs once on load: build the page, check the session, register the service worker.

recap.title: Skeleton first, data second
recap.body: component() builds empty containers. restoreFromStorage() fills them.

recap.title: Local paint, then cloud
recap.body: The screen draws from localStorage before Supabase answers, so the app opens instantly.

recap.title: Boot runs once
recap.body: bootApp guards itself, so a second auth event can't start the app twice.

steps.title: The page skeleton is built first.
steps.why: Before anyone is signed in, index.js builds the whole page and attaches it to the body.

steps.title: component() makes the empty layout.
steps.why: Nav bar, sidebar, list and footer are created here, still with no projects in them.

steps.title: Signed in? Boot. Otherwise, the sign-in modal.
steps.why: The saved session decides the path. No session means the sign-in form covers the page.

steps.title: bootApp paints from localStorage first.
steps.why: Your projects appear straight away from this device's copy. The cloud catches up after.

steps.title: restoreFromStorage draws the sidebar and list.
steps.why: One sidebar row per project, then the selected project's todos in the main list.

steps.title: Then sync: migrate, hydrate, subscribe.
steps.why: Upload old local data once, pull everything from Supabase, then listen for live changes.

recap.title: One shared client
recap.body: supabaseClient.js makes the only Supabase client. Every file imports it.

recap.title: Missing keys never crash
recap.body: Without build-time keys a stub client answers with empty data.

recap.title: Email codes, no passwords
recap.body: sendCode emails a one-time code. verifyCode turns it into a session.

recap.title: The session gates every write
recap.body: persistMutation and hydrate both stop when nobody is signed in.

steps.title: One client, built from build-time keys.
steps.why: Webpack bakes the URL and public key in. The session is saved and refreshed for you.

steps.title: No keys? A stub keeps the app running.
steps.why: It answers every call with empty data, so a local build still opens, signed out.

match: return { ok: false, message: 'No account for that email' };
steps.title: Sign-in starts with an emailed code.
steps.why: Only existing accounts get one. Errors become short messages for the form.

steps.title: The code is swapped for a session.
steps.why: Supabase checks the code. On success the client now holds a signed-in session.

steps.title: Auth changes boot the app or tear it down.
steps.why: A new session hides the modal and boots. Signing out clears data and shows it again.

steps.title: Every write checks the session first.
steps.why: Projects carry your user_id. Todos don't: their access is checked through their project.

steps.title: Hydrate reads everything back.
steps.why: Your projects, then all todos you can see. The database only returns rows you own.

tours.title: Signing in for the first time

recap.title: Ask the cloud before onboarding
recap.body: A user with cloud projects skips the sample project and the tour.

recap.title: Migration runs once per user
recap.body: A marker in localStorage records that this device already uploaded.

recap.title: Cloud wins when it has data
recap.body: Local data only uploads into an empty account.

recap.title: Sign-out wipes this device
recap.body: Local projects and the marker go, so the next user starts clean.

steps.title: Boot first asks: do you already have data?
steps.why: The answer decides onboarding, and is passed on so the migration needn't ask again.

steps.title: Existing users skip the welcome.
steps.why: Cloud projects found? Onboarding is marked done. A timeout stops a slow check blocking the page.

steps.title: The probe fetches one project id.
steps.why: One row is enough to know. It returns null on errors, meaning 'couldn't tell'.

steps.title: Local data moves up once per user.
steps.why: Only into an empty account. The marker is set afterwards, so it never runs twice.

steps.title: Each project goes up, then its todos.
steps.why: Parents first, so every todo has a project to belong to. Blank rows are skipped.

steps.title: Signing out clears this device.
steps.why: Projects and the migration marker are removed, so the next person sees none of it.

recap.title: Memory first, always
recap.body: Edits change the item in memory straight away. Saving follows.

recap.title: Typing is batched
recap.body: saveToStorageSoon waits a moment, so a burst of keys is one write.

recap.title: dataChanged tells the UI
recap.body: Every local save fires it, so badges and counts refresh.

recap.title: Two names for every field
recap.body: toTodoRowPayload maps tit / desc / due to title / description / due_date.

recap.title: Parents land first
recap.body: A todo write waits for its project's insert to finish.

steps.title: Each keystroke updates the item in memory.
steps.why: The title changes on the item right away. The save to disk is asked for, not done.

steps.title: Saves while typing are combined.
steps.why: One timer at a time: fast typing becomes a single write instead of one per key.

steps.title: All projects go to localStorage.
steps.why: The whole model is written under one key, then dataChanged tells the UI to refresh.

steps.title: Memory names become column names.
steps.why: The app says tit, desc and due. The database says title, description and due_date.

steps.title: A todo waits for its project to exist.
steps.why: If the project's insert is still in flight, the todo write waits, so it's never orphaned.

steps.title: Insert or update, and note our own echo.
steps.why: New rows insert, edits update. noteSelfEcho lets realtime skip the copy we just sent.

recap.title: Realtime updates the data
recap.body: Supabase pushes each change; listLogic applies it to memory and storage.

recap.title: Re-sync repaints the screen
recap.body: hydrateFromSupabase pulls everything, then fires listLogicHydrated.

recap.title: Never while you type
recap.body: A re-sync is skipped while an input has focus.

recap.title: Last write wins
recap.body: When both sides changed, the newer updated_at is kept.

steps.title: Two live channels: projects and todos.
steps.why: Supabase pushes every insert, update and delete on those tables to this device.

steps.title: A pushed change is applied to memory.
steps.why: Our own echoes are skipped. Others are added, updated or removed, then saved locally.

steps.title: A full re-sync, but never while you type.
steps.why: Repainting would wipe a half-typed edit, so focus in an input skips this round.

steps.title: When re-syncs happen.
steps.why: Tab visible again, window focus or back online. A 5-minute timer is the backstop.

steps.title: Merge: last write wins.
steps.why: The newer side wins. Local todos the server hasn't confirmed yet are kept, not lost.

match: restoreFromStorage({ fromSync: true, selectProject: activeProject || undefined });
steps.title: The screen repaints, same project selected.
steps.why: Sidebar and list are rebuilt from the merged data, keeping the project you had open.

recap.title: The service worker caches the build
recap.body: Files load from cache, so the app opens offline. The page itself checks the network first.

recap.title: A new build waits
recap.body: It installs in the background and waits until you choose to reload.

recap.title: Two cues, one path
recap.body: The mobile pill and the About row both call applyPendingUpdate.

recap.title: Only the tapping tab reloads
recap.body: Other open tabs get a 'Reload to finish' cue instead.

steps.title: The service worker caches the whole build.
steps.why: Old caches are dropped. Pages try the network first; everything else loads from cache.

steps.title: The page registers it and watches for builds.
steps.why: A new worker waiting means an update. Checks run on load, on return and hourly.

steps.title: Checks can also be forced.
steps.why: When a run ships, the assistant asks for a check now instead of waiting for the next poll.

steps.title: Phones get an 'Update available' pill.
steps.why: It sits above the bottom nav, appears once, and stays away for the session if dismissed.

steps.title: Settings › About shows the same cue.
steps.why: The Version row gets its own pill. Tapping it takes the same path as the mobile one.

steps.title: Both cues share one reload path.
steps.why: Mark this tab as the one that asked, then tell the waiting worker to take over.

steps.title: The new worker takes over; this tab reloads.
steps.why: Only the tab that asked reloads. Other open tabs get a 'Reload to finish' cue instead.

recap.title: listLogic is the only thing that changes data
recap.body: UI code edits the item, then asks listLogic to save it.

recap.title: Two places hold your data
recap.body: localStorage first (instant), Supabase second through persistMutation.

recap.title: One blank row, always
recap.body: Real in memory, never saved to the database.

recap.title: Two names for every field
recap.body: Memory says tit / desc / due. The database says title / description / due_date.

recap.title: Sync has two layers
recap.body: Realtime updates the data. Re-sync repaints the screen.

steps.title: One empty row always sits on top.
steps.why: It's a real item in memory, but it never gets saved to the server.

steps.title: Typing doesn't save the empty row.
steps.why: A half-typed title can't become a task if you switch projects mid-word.

steps.title: Enter: save locally, then insert or update.
steps.why: First commit inserts. Later edits update. Re-inserting used to cause duplicate errors.

steps.title: The row gets an id and is sent off.
steps.why: Blank titles are refused here too, so the empty row can never slip through.

steps.title: The one door to the database.
steps.why: Every write in the app passes here. Signed out? It stops, and the task stays local.

steps.title: A fresh empty row appears.
steps.why: The cursor jumps into it, so you can type the next task right away.

steps.title: Other devices receive the new row.
steps.why: The device that made it ignores its own echo. Others save it locally.

steps.title: Their screen repaints on re-sync.
steps.why: Not instantly: when the tab becomes visible again, or every 5 minutes.
